summary: The baseline grep `^Skill-Diet: <name>\b` also matches trailers for any skill whose name extends this one after a hyphen (qa vs qa-only, review vs review-voice). A diet commit for the longer-named skill that also touches this skill's folder becomes this skill's baseline, so growthPct and the DUE flag are wrong.
evidence: Scratch repo with qa/ and qa-only/; a commit touching qa/SKILL.md with the trailer 'Skill-Diet: qa-only'; `bin/gstack-skill-bill ./qa` printed 'BASELINE: 4d07983 2026-11-01 SKILL.md 63 B; now +3.2%' instead of 'BASELINE: none'. `\b` matches between 'qa' and '-only'.

summary: The new mode table gives the commands as bare `gstack-learnings-search ...` / `gstack-learnings-log ...`. The install bin folder is not on PATH, so an agent that runs a row literally gets 'command not found'; the removed sections used full <home>/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/ paths. The drift scanner also skips these rows because it needs a bin/ prefix.
evidence: Table rows such as '| stats | `gstack-learnings-search --stats` |'; `grep -n PATH learn/SKILL.md` finds no PATH export; BIN_RE in scripts/skill-bin-drift.ts requires a `bin/` (or similar) prefix.

summary: The new /learn mode table writes every command as a bare name (`gstack-learnings-search --stats`, `gstack-learnings-log '<json>'`, ...). gstack's bin/ isn't on PATH, so these fail if run as written, and the new drift checker only matches calls written with a bin/ path, so it never checks this table's flags. /write-skill section 4 and references/diet.md do the same with `gstack-skill-bill`.
evidence: In a scratch repo, a /learn template passing a fake `--statz` flag in a bare-name table row (line 6) and in a full-path code block (line 9): `bun run scripts/skill-bin-drift.ts --root $D --skill learn` reported only `DRIFT_UNKNOWN_FLAG learn/SKILL.md.tmpl:9 ... --statz`; the table row was missed. setup and the /learn preamble never add the gstack bin dir to PATH.
